**Proposed mechanism:** SLC6A6 (HGNC:11176) —DECREASES→ Taurine (CHEBI:17471); SLC6A6 (HGNC:11176) —DISRUPTS→ Amino acid transport (GO:0005319); Taurine (CHEBI:17471) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547); Taurine (CHEBI:17471) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); SLC7A9 (HGNC:11179) —DECREASES→ Cystine (CHEBI:17900); SLC3A1 (HGNC:11170) —DECREASES→ Cystine (CHEBI:17900); SLC7A9 (HGNC:11179) —DISRUPTS→ Amino acid transport (GO:0005319); SLC3A1 (HGNC:11170) —DISRUPTS→ Amino acid transport (GO:0005319); Cystine (CHEBI:17900) —LEADS_TO→ Cystinuria (HP:0000043); Amino acid transport (GO:0005319) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000547); Amino acid transport (GO:0005319) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638). Mutations in SLC6A6 lead to reduced cellular taurine levels, causing hypotaurinemic retinal degeneration and cardiomyopathy. Concurrently, mutations in SLC7A9 and SLC3A1 impair cystine transport, leading to cystinuria. Both diseases converge on the broader pathway of amino acid transport, with specific dysregulation of taurine and cystine impacting distinct cellular functions and leading to the observed phenotypes.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of individuals with pathogenic variants in SLC6A6 who do not exhibit retinal degeneration or cardiomyopathy, or individuals with pathogenic variants in SLC7A9/SLC3A1 who do not present with cystinuria, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exclusion of pathogenic variants in gnomAD for the specified causal genes in unaffected individuals.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of amino acid transporters in these distinct diseases could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting amino acid metabolism or transporter function for both conditions. For example, interventions aimed at restoring taurine levels or managing cystine accumulation might offer therapeutic benefits.

#### 2. Hartnup disease  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.421)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-352230)

**Proposed mechanism:** SLC6A6 (HGNC:10620) —DISRUPTS→ Taurine transport (GO:0015894); Taurine transport (GO:0015894) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000506); Taurine transport (GO:0015894) —LEADS_TO→ Cardiomyopathy (HP:0001638); SLC6A19 (HGNC:10623) —DISRUPTS→ Neutral amino acid transport (GO:0015721); Neutral amino acid transport (GO:0015721) —DECREASES→ Tryptophan (CHEBI:17640); Tryptophan (CHEBI:17640) —DECREASES→ Indole derivatives (CHEBI:17772); Indole derivatives (CHEBI:17772) —LEADS_TO→ Ataxia (HP:0001251); Indole derivatives (CHEBI:17772) —LEADS_TO→ Photosensitivity (HP:0001090). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC6A6 disrupt taurine transport, leading to hypotaurinemic retinal degeneration and cardiomyopathy. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SLC6A19 disrupt neutral amino acid transport, specifically affecting tryptophan uptake. This reduced tryptophan transport leads to decreased production of indole derivatives, which are implicated in neurological and dermatological phenotypes such as ataxia and photosensitivity seen in Hartnup disease. The convergence is at the level of disrupted amino acid and related metabolite transport pathways.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of significant overlap in the molecular pathways affected by SLC6A6 and SLC6A19 mutations, or identification of distinct and unrelated molecular mechanisms for each disease. _(variant: Identification of a common, highly prevalent pathogenic variant in both SLC6A6 and SLC6A19 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared genetic basis in amino acid transport could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting common metabolic pathways or transporters to mitigate symptoms in both conditions.
